The study analyzed bonded composite repairs for cracked aluminum aircraft structures using finite element method
Two repair configurations were studied: one with different adhesive shear moduli and one with different adhesive thicknesses
Maximum SIF reduction of 39% was achieved when comparing Ga1 = 1000 MPa to Ga2 = 100 MPa
The aluminum plate dimensions were 254mm × 254mm × 3mm with Young's modulus of 72 GPa
The Boron-Epoxy composite patch dimensions were 127mm × 127mm × 2mm
Applied uniaxial tensile stress on the aluminum plate was 70 MPa
The finite element mesh contained 25,567 eight-noded isoparametric elements
Adhesive thickness in Configuration 1 was 0.2mm for both bands
In Configuration 2, adhesive thicknesses ranged from 0.1mm to 0.2mm for the first band
The height of the adhesive band had negligible effect on SIF reduction
SIF reduction between Ga1 = 400 MPa and 600 MPa was approximately 8.74%
SIF reduction between Ga1 = 800 MPa and 1000 MPa was only about 5%
For small cracks (less than 10mm), the two-adhesive-band repair was not effective
Maximum adhesive shear stress σxz was 5.26 MPa at Ga1 = 400 MPa and 11.22 MPa at Ga1 = 1000 MPa
The ratio of maximum σxz stresses between Ga1 = 1000 MPa and 400 MPa was 2.1
Adhesive thickness reduction from 0.2mm to 0.1mm resulted in approximately 15% SIF reduction
The practical range for adhesive thickness in the two-band configuration was 0.1-0.2mm
The modified crack closure method was used to calculate stress intensity factors
Plane stress conditions were assumed in the finite element analysis
The adhesive was modeled as homogeneous, linear elastic, and isotropic material
Surface shear stresses in the adhesive were proportional to relative displacements between layers
The study used Franc2D/L finite element code developed at Kansas University
Boron-Epoxy patch had longitudinal Young's modulus of 210 GPa and transversal Young's modulus of 19.6 GPa
The composite patch shear modulus was 5.46 GPa
Adhesive shear modulus values tested ranged from 100 MPa to 1000 MPa
